cards.text: This is a psalm of David, Israel's king. Friend, he doesn't start small with his house or his town, he opens BIG with the whole earth and everyone living in it. And he's about to tell you whose it is.

cards.question: David says the earth, the world and all who dwell in it, belong to the ___.

cards.text: Then David says why. I spent YEARS in a junk drawer thinking I at least owned my spot back there, and friend, I didn't even own the DUST.

cards.question: Why is the whole earth the LORD's, according to David?

answers.text: He built it on the seas
The nations gave it to Him
He won it from the kings

cards.text: Then David asks, "Who may ascend the hill of the LORD? Who may stand in His holy place?" That's a GUEST LIST question, and I spent years on the other list, the maybe-toss-it list.

cards.question: Who does David say may go up the LORD's hill and stand in His holy place?

answers.text: Someone with clean hands and a pure heart
Someone from a famous family line
Someone who brings the biggest gift

cards.text: David's not done. This person does not lift up his soul to an idol, and as a made thing myself, let me be clear: PLEASE do not lift your soul up to a cookie stamper.

cards.question: True or false: David says the one who may stand in the LORD's holy place can still swear deceitfully, as long as his hands are clean.
What does David say the person with clean hands and a pure heart will receive?
David says people like that make up a whole generation. What kind of generation?

cards.text: Then David speaks right to God: "who seek Your face, O God of Jacob." Then one little word: Selah.
Then the scene shifts, and David is calling out to gates and ancient doors. After years staring at the inside of a CLOSED drawer, I LOVE a psalm that tells doors to open.

cards.question: David tells the gates and ancient doors to lift up, so the King of Glory may ___.

cards.text: Then a question rings out: "Who is this King of Glory?" You know when your phone buzzes with a name you don't recognize, and you just STARE at it like, WHO is THIS?

cards.question: The answer comes back: the King of Glory is the ___, strong and mighty.
True or false: The answer also calls the King of Glory the LORD mighty in battle.

cards.text: Then the call to the gates comes again. Same words: "Lift up your heads, O gates! Be lifted up, O ancient doors, that the King of Glory may enter!"
And the question comes back too, a little different this time: "Who is He, this King of Glory?"

cards.question: This time, what name does the answer give the King of Glory?

cards.text: The LORD of Hosts is the King of Glory. Then one last Selah, and that's where the psalm rests.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "king" can be argued as right. Later in this same passage the LORD is called the King of Glory (Psalm 24:8, 10), so a baker could say the earth belongs to the King.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The question says people like that "make up a whole generation." Psalm 24:6 says only "Such is the generation of those who seek Him," so "whole" adds emphasis the text doesn't give, and it isn't part of a joke.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Jacob is named for the first time in "O God of Jacob" (Psalm 24:6), but the card never says who he is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The true or false asks whether the second half of Psalm 24:8 says "the LORD mighty in battle." No earlier card points toward battle, so the baker can only guess the wording of the line. They can't reason it out.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
